Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.gli!gßlov.ph otLG OPINION NO. 72 s. 2020 JUN 1 1 2025 ATTY. ARVIN A. ODRON Regional Director Commission on Human Rights Region VII 132 F. Rafanan Building, Don Mariano Cui St. Capitol Site, Cebu City Dear Dir. Odron: This has reference to your letter seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the obligation of local government units to provide relocation to their residents affected by demolition and orders to vacate government property and privately-owned lots, particularly the following queries: I. Prevailing rule and policy of the Government whether LGUs have a demandable obligation to provide adequate relocation to its residents affected by demolitions and order to vacate; 2. What conditions would trigger this obligation/s to set in, and 3. What are the limitations, if any? As to the first and second queries. we will answer them in one discussion as they are interrelated. Please be informed that the prevailing rule is the Section 28 (8) of R.A. 7279, otherwise known as the Urban Development and Housing Act (UDHA) which mandates the Local Government Units, together with the National Housing Authority to relocate the underprivileged and homeless citizens affected by eviction and demolition. Section 28, Article VII of RA 7279 states: SEC. 28. Eviction and Demolition. — Eviction or demolition as a practice shall be discouraged. Eviction or demolition, however, may be allowed under the following situations: (a) When persons or entities occupy danger areas such as esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, and other public places such as sidewalks, roads, parks, and playgrounds; (b) When government infrastructure projects with available funding are about to be implemented; or (c) When there is a court order for eviction and demolition. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In the execution of eviction or demolition orders involving underprivileged and homeless citizens, the following shall be mandatory: (I) Notice upon the affected persons or entities at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of eviction or demolition; (2) Adequate consultations on the matter of resettlement with the duly designated representatives of the families to be resettled and the affected communities in the areas where they are to be relocated; (3) Presence of local government officials or their representatives during eviction or demolition; (4) Proper identification of all persons taking part in the demolition; (5) Execution of eviction or demolition only during regular office hours from Mondays to Fridays and during good weather, unless the affected families consent otherwise; (6) No use of heavy equipment for demolition except for structures that are permanent and of concrete materials; (7) Proper uniforms for members of the Philippine National Police who shall occupy the first line of law enforcement and observe proper disturbance control procedures; and (8) Adequate relocation, whether temporary or permanent: Provided, however, That in cases of eviction and demolition pursuant to a court order involving underprivileged and homeless citizens, relocation shall be undertaken by the local qovernment unit concerned and the National Housinq Authority with the assistance of other government agencies within forty-five (45) days from service of notice of final judgment by the court, after which period the said order shall be executed: Provided, further, That should relocation not be possible within the said period. financial assistance in the amount equivalent to the prevailing minimum daily wage multiplied by sixty (60) days shall be extended to the affected families by the local government unit concern Xxxx" (R.A. 7279) (Emphasis ours) Also, the Supreme Court, in the case of Galay V. CA and Wongi, ruled: "The aforecited provision is very explicit that the task of relocating the homeless and the underprivileqed shall be the responsibility of the local government unit concerned and the National Housinq Authority with the assistance of the other government aqencies. Although private individuals are not prohibited from taking part in the relocation, there is nothing in the law either that compels them to undertake such task on a mandatory basis, otherwise, such obligation G.R. No. 120132 December 4, 1995 Page 2 of 3

should have been included in the provision, either expressly or impliedly." (Emphasis ours) In connection with this, it is imperative to define who are considered "underprivileged and homeless". Thus, we invite your attention to Section 3 (t) of R.A. 7279 which provides: "(t) "Underprivileged and homeless citizens" refers to the beneficiaries of this Act and to individuals or families residing in urban and urbanizable areas whose income or combined household income falls within the poverty threshold as defined by the National Economic and Development Authority and who do not own housing facilities. This shall include those who live in makeshift dwelling units and do not enjoy security of tenure;" From the foregoing, it is clear that the LGUs and the NHA, with the assistance of other government agencies, have the responsibility of providing adequate relocation to its residents affected by demolitions and order to vacate. Provided, that the relocation is only for the affected residents which are considered underprivileged and homeless. In accordance with this policy, the aforementioned provision states that eviction or demolition as a practice is discouraged. It, however, provides situations where eviction or demolition is allowed but prescribes requirements that must be satisfied before an eviction or demolitions involving underprivileged and homeless citizens are considered valid.2 Thus, relocation of underprivileged and homeless would set in if they are affected by eviction or demolition under the situations stated in Section 28 of RA 7279. As to the third query, the limitations under Section 28 of RA 7279 are that the relocation should be done within forty-five (45) days from service of notice of final judgment by the court, or in case relocation is not possible, within the said period, financial assistance in the amount equivalent to the prevailing minimum daily wage multiplied by sixty (60) days shall be extended to the affected families by the local government unit concern. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, ROMEO . BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB,'LLLS-LRALLDnasm copy Furnished: LEOCADIO T.
